info.title: Brigade API
info.description:
Brigade's public HTTP API: what an integration may call. Incidents and the catalog (services,
incident types, custom fields) are read and changed here too, each write through the same named mutation the apps
send, with the same rules, timeline entries and events. Everything else (monitors, schedules, escalation policies,
devices) is read and changed over Brigade Sync, the WebSocket `openSync` opens (RFC 0004). Routes not listed here
are internal and may change without notice.

**Auth.** A Better Auth session: sign in with `POST /api/auth/sign-in/email` (`{ "email", "password" }`) and send
the cookie it sets. Writes that carry a cookie refuse another site's `Origin` (`403 forbidden_origin`); a request
without `Origin` is not refused for it. Operations marked with `bearerAuth` also take an API token (RFC 0014): an
owner or admin mints one in the dashboard for one workspace, with scopes, and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer
brg_…`. A token acts with its creator's role as it is now and only within its scopes (`403 forbidden` otherwise);
every refused token (wrong, revoked, expired, its creator gone) is the same `401 unauthenticated`; a token's requests
are limited (`429 rate_limited`, `Retry-After`). A bearer request skips the `Origin` check and ignores any cookie.

**Errors.** Every refusal is JSON, `{ "error": "<code>" }`, with the codes each operation lists. Any other method on
a listed path answers `405` with `Allow`; an unknown path `404 not_found`.

**Webhooks.** What Brigade sends to the endpoints a workspace registers: a signed `POST` per event, as the Standard
Webhooks specification has it (`@freecorps/brigade-sdk`'s `verifyWebhook`, or any of its libraries, verifies
it). Each payload is `version: 1`; fields may be added to it, so ignore the ones you do not know. A change that
is not purely additive is a new version. See RFC 0005 "Outbound webhooks".

post.summary: Send alerts to an alert source
post.description: What Grafana, Datadog, Sentry or any webhook posts (RFC 0005 "Alert sources"). The token is the source URL's last segment (shown once, when the source is made or its URL rotated). The body is the provider's own payload, at most 256 KiB; a Sentry source also needs `Sentry-Hook-Signature`, a Grafana source with an HMAC secret `X-Grafana-Alerting-Signature`, and a source with a header that header. A payload Brigade cannot read is still accepted (`malformed`), and pages. So is one past 256 KiB, unread (`tooLarge`): it pages one unreadable alert once the URL and the source's header check out (a signature needs the body, so the secret URL authenticates it). Every refusal of the URL, header or signature is the same `404`; `503` carries `Retry-After` (over a rate limit too: Datadog retries a 5xx, not a 429; and for a token refused within the last minute once the workspace's refusals are over their limit).

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: `<workspaceId>.<sourceId>.<secret>`, from the alert source's URL.

202.description: Accepted: how many alerts it held, whether it was unreadable, and whether it was too large to read.

get.description: Newest first (by id: when the declaring client made it), 50 a page by default. Every member may read them. Filters combine; `status` and `severity` take a comma-separated list. `nextCursor` is the next page's `cursor`, null on the last. A request reads at most 1000 incidents: past that it answers the page so far, maybe short or empty, with a `nextCursor` where it stopped, so follow `nextCursor` until it is null rather than stopping at a short page. With an API token: the `incident:read` scope.

post.description: Runs `incident.declare` as the member (responders and up), as declaring in the app does: numbered, on the timeline, `incident.declared` through the outbox, and paged by the escalation policy exactly as a declare from the dashboard is. The severity defaults to the type's, else `sev3`; a type or service that does not exist is left out, as in the app. `escalationPolicyId` picks the policy that pages it, first in the order (RFC 0006 "Who is paged"); one that does not exist, or is deleted before the page, falls back to the usual order. With an API token: the `incident:declare` scope.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Your id for this request (1 to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `:` or `-`), so a retry after a lost answer runs it once: the same key with the same request again, within 7 days, answers what the first request did (a create, the same entry; a refusal, the same refusal) and changes nothing more. The key is tied to that request (its route, target and body): sent with another one it is `422 idempotency_key_reused` and runs nothing. A key is the caller's own: another member or token reusing it makes a new request.

patch.summary: Change an incident's title, type, services, fields, roles, severity or status
patch.description: Each change is its own named mutation, as in the app, in this order: `incident.rename`, `incident.setType`, `incident.setServices`, `incident.setField` per field, `incident.assignRole` per role, `incident.setSeverity`, `incident.setStatus` (each with its timeline entry and event). One that asks for what already is changes nothing. The first refusal stops the rest and is the answer; the changes before it stay made. The same request with the same key answers the same refusal again (results are kept, refusals too); once what refused it is fixed, send it with a new key: the changes already made come back as changing nothing, and the rest run. Responders and up. `409 invalid_transition`: the status cannot follow the current one. `400 invalid_args` with an issue at `roles.<role id>`: a role the workspace does not offer, or someone who is not a member or is a viewer. The answer is the incident, so an API token needs `incident:read` too. With an API token: the `incident:update` and `incident:read` scopes.

parameters.description: The workspace (`ws_<ULID>`).

parameters.description: The incident (`inc_<ULID>`).

The key is tied to that request (its route, target and body): sent with another one it is `422 idempotency_key_reused` and runs nothing. A key is the caller's own: another member or token reusing it makes a new request.

patch.description: Runs `incident.editUpdate`: the update's text changes in place (it keeps its place, time and author, and reads "edited"), in any status. Only its author: the member who posted it, or an API token that posted it or whose creator did; anyone else is `403 forbidden`, owners and admins included. Text it already has changes nothing. `409 conflict`: the update was removed. `404 not_found`: no such update on this incident. What was published on the status page is never changed by it. With an API token: the `incident:update` scope.
